content: I'll start by reading the test image to identify key visual features.

The test image shows:
- Tomato stems with severe wilting and "shepherd's crook" drooping tips
- Dark brown/black necrotic stem cankers at a node junction
- Mummified/shriveled tissue at the base of the wilted stems
- Green healthy leaves in background

Top candidates: **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato**, **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**, **Phytophthora_Blight**, **Bacterial_Wilt**

Now I'll read one reference image from each of my top 4 candidates.
This Bacterial_Canker reference shows internal stem discoloration - doesn't match the test image's dark external cankers. Let me check Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers.
That Alternaria reference is a microscopy image - not helpful for macroscopic comparison. Let me check Phytophthora_Blight and Bacterial_Wilt.
The Phytophthora reference shows dark stem lesions on pepper - some similarity. Let me use my last view on another Alternaria reference to see macroscopic symptoms.

Excellent - the Alternaria Bugwood_4 reference is highly informative. It shows a dark black/brown stem canker at the base with the stem curling upward (shepherd's crook). This is a strong visual match to the test image.

**Analysis summary:**

| Feature | Test Image | Alternaria Stem Cankers | Bacterial Canker | Phytophthora |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dark black/brown stem cankers | ✓ | ✓ Strong match | Partial | Partial |
| Shepherd's crook wilting of shoots | ✓ | ✓ Present | ✓ Classic | Rare |
| Mummified/shriveled tissue at base | ✓ | ✓ | Partial | Possible |
| Node/junction location | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

The Alternaria Bugwood_4 reference (5530065) shows nearly identical features to the test image:
- Very dark (near-black) stem canker tissue
- The shoot above the canker curves/droops in a shepherd's crook
- Dried necrotic tissue at the lesion base

The bacterial canker reference showed internal vascular discoloration rather than the dark external canker seen in the test image. The test image's deeply darkened, charcoal-colored stem necrosis concentrated at a stem junction, combined with the shepherd's crook wilting of multiple shoots emanating from that junction, is most consistent with **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**.
